findings.title: Ensure permissions on /etc/shadow are configured
findings.evidence: Insecure permissions: 666 owner root:root (expected 640 root:shadow or root:root)

findings.title: Ensure no accounts have empty password fields
Ensure firewall is active
findings.command: ufw status 2>/dev/null || systemctl is-active firewalld 2>/dev/null || iptables -L -n 2>/dev/null

findings.title: Ensure sudoers contains no NOPASSWD wildcard
findings.evidence: NOPASSWD entry found: %sudo ALL=(ALL:ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL

findings.title: Ensure no world-writable files exist in system paths
Ensure password complexity / length policy is set
Ensure automatic security updates are enabled

fix_list.finding: Permissions or ownership on /etc/shadow are insecure. (Observed: 'Insecure permissions: 666 owner root:root (expected 640 root:shadow or root:root)')
fix_list.why_it_matters: /etc/shadow contains encrypted user password hashes. Excessive permissions allow local password hash cracking.

fix_list.finding: Accounts with empty password fields detected. (Observed: 'Account(s) with empty password: testuser')
fix_list.why_it_matters: Allows unauthenticated users to gain shell access without entering a password.

fix_list.finding: Root login over SSH is permitted. (Observed: 'PermitRootLogin is set to 'yes' (expected 'no')')
fix_list.why_it_matters: A leaked or brute-forced root credential grants full remote access with no separate privilege escalation step.
fix_list.fix_command: sudo sed -i 's/^PermitRootLogin.*/PermitRootLogin no/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config && sudo systemctl reload sshd

fix_list.finding: Wildcard NOPASSWD found in sudoers configuration. (Observed: 'NOPASSWD entry found: %sudo ALL=(ALL:ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL')
fix_list.why_it_matters: Allows users or compromised processes to run administrative commands as root without authentication.
fix_list.fix_command: sudo visudo  # Remove NOPASSWD directives from /etc/sudoers and /etc/sudoers.d/

fix_list.finding: SSH password authentication is enabled. (Observed: 'PasswordAuthentication is set to 'yes' (expected 'no')')
fix_list.why_it_matters: Allows password brute-force attacks against SSH service. Key-based authentication should be enforced.
fix_list.fix_command: sudo sed -i 's/^PasswordAuthentication.*/PasswordAuthentication no/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config && sudo systemctl reload sshd

fix_list.finding: World-writable files present in system directories. (Observed: 'World-writable files detected: /etc/config_backup.tmp')
fix_list.why_it_matters: Any local user can modify or corrupt critical system configuration or executable scripts.

fix_list.finding: Automatic security updates are disabled. (Observed: 'Automatic security updates disabled')
fix_list.why_it_matters: Leaves system unpatched against publicly known security vulnerabilities (CVEs).
fix_list.fix_command: sudo apt-get install -y unattended-upgrades && sudo dpkg-reconfigure --priority=low unattended-upgrades

fix_list.finding: Password complexity / length policy is insufficient. (Observed: 'Minimum password length is 6 (expected >= 14)')
fix_list.why_it_matters: Short or simple passwords are vulnerable to dictionary and brute-force attacks.
fix_list.fix_command: sudo apt-get install -y libpam-pwquality && sudo sed -i 's/# minlen =.*/minlen = 14/' /etc/security/pwquality.conf

firewall_status.command: ufw status 2>/dev/null || systemctl is-active firewalld 2>/dev/null || iptables -L -n 2>/dev/null
